newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CVRD sale may be delayed - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CVRD sale may be delayed - paper.

text.p: The first phase of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce's privatization, which was expected to start in February, may be delayed until March, a top official of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) said.

The Folha de S. Paulo quoted BNDES vice president Pio Borges as saying the goal of holding a February auction of an initial 45-percent stake in the firm was "ambitious" and might be set for March instead.
The paper quoted Borges as saying the extra time might be needed to allow potential investors time to visit and study CVRD, the world's largest iron ore producer.
"We want interested parties to feel comfortable so that they will bid the maximum price possible," he said.
Nonetheless, the auction would not be delayed beyond the first quarter of 1997, Borges was quoted as saying.

His comments come just days after two former presidents, Senate chief Jose Sarney and Itamar Franco, proclaimed their opposition to CVRD's transfer to private hands, raising fears the selloff will be tripped up in Congress.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has vowed the privatisation will proceed and will not be used to bargain for congressional votes in favor of his bid to stand for re-election in 1997.
